notes: Class games: quick challenges a teacher throws at the class on most school days (a few seconds each). Each setup is one way it can happen: which game, which classes it fits, what the teacher says, and how it lands. {period}, {class_name}, {teacher} and {them_first} (a classmate) are filled in. The games themselves are in data/minigames.json (class: true); the banks below are what the order and odd-one-out games are made of. Facts must be correct.
pass: {them_first} goes for it instead. Close, not quite. They shrug all the way back to their seat.
{them_first} takes it and nails it, then looks right at you like: your turn next time.
{them_first} gets up there. The class cheers either way, and {them_first} bows.
sit: You draw a pretty solid dog in the margin. Class moves on.
You watch someone else go. Honestly, more relaxing.
You zone out for a minute. Nobody notices. Probably.

setups.title: Fill it to the line
text: {period}, {class_name}. {teacher} sets a beaker on the front desk. "Fill it to the line. Closest one skips tonight's worksheet."
{period}, {class_name}. {teacher} holds up a graduated cylinder. "Twenty-five milliliters. Exactly. Who's got steady hands?"
setups.how: Hold to pour. Let go on the line.
great: Dead on the line. {teacher} holds it up to the light and nods. "Worksheet's off for you."
Exactly on the mark. Somebody in the back actually claps.
good: A hair over. {teacher} squints at it. "I'll allow it."
miss: It overflows onto the desk. {them_first} hands you paper towels, cracking up.
Way short. {teacher}: "That's a rounding error with ambition."

setups.title: How many atoms?
text: {period}, {class_name}. {teacher} writes formulas on the board, fast. "How many atoms in each one? Call it."
{period}. {teacher} slaps a stack of formula cards on the desk. "Count the atoms. Beat {them_first} and you pick the lab partners."
setups.how: Count the atoms. Tap the answer.
great: You rattle them off before {teacher} finishes writing. "Okay. Okay," {teacher} says.
Perfect run. {them_first} turns around in their seat like, how?
good: Most of them. Glucose got you, but glucose gets everyone.
miss: Those little numbers move when you look at them. You swear.
You count the H's twice and the O's never. Next time.

setups.title: Periodic order
text: {period}, {class_name}. {teacher} deals out element cards. "Atomic number order. Go."
{period}. "Line these up by atomic number," {teacher} says. "Fastest table gets the good goggles."
setups.how: Tap them lowest atomic number first.
great: Clean sweep. Your table gets the good goggles.
{teacher} checks your cards. "Every one. Nice."
good: Close. One swap off, and {teacher} lets it slide.
Mostly right. You'll remember iron now.
miss: You put gold before carbon with total confidence.
{them_first} quietly fixes your order for you.

setups.title: Find the mutation
text: {period}, {class_name}. {teacher} projects a wall of DNA. "One of these has a mutation. Find it before {them_first} does."
{period}. "Somewhere in here, one base is wrong," says {teacher}. "Eyes up. Go."
great: You spot it instantly. {teacher}: "Somebody's going into genetics."
Three for three, before anyone else even squints.
good: Got most of them. The last one was sneaky.
Not bad. {them_first} got one you missed and won't let you forget it.
miss: They all look the same. They all look exactly the same.
You tap the wrong one with your whole chest.

setups.title: Smallest to biggest
text: {period}, {class_name}. {teacher} hands out cards: a virus, a cell, an ant, a whale. "By size. Smallest first."
{period}. "Scale check," {teacher} says, dealing size cards. "Smallest first. Fastest table gets the good microscope."
great: Every card in the right place. The good microscope is yours.
{teacher} nods slowly. "That's the whole unit, right there."
good: One mix-up. You'll get it on the test.
miss: You put the whale second. You will be hearing about that.
{them_first} leans over: "A virus is not bigger than a cell, man."

setups.title: Levels of life
text: {period}, {class_name}. "Levels of life," {teacher} says, dealing cards. "Cell up to biosphere. Go."
{period}. {teacher}: "Organization, smallest level first. You versus {them_first}."
great: Every level in place. {teacher}: "That's the whole unit, right there."
Clean. You beat {them_first} by a full level.
good: One swap. Community and population are close.
miss: You put the ecosystem inside a cell.
{them_first} leans over: "Tissue comes before organ, man."

setups.title: Mental math race
text: {period}, {class_name}. {teacher} clicks a stopwatch. "Five problems, no calculators. Beat my time and you're off homework."
{period}. "Around the world," {teacher} says. "You're up against {them_first}. Go."
great: You beat the stopwatch. {teacher} actually looks impressed.
You take {them_first} down five straight. Polite applause.
good: Respectable. {teacher} writes your time on the board anyway.
miss: Seven times eight. You knew it. You KNEW it.
Your brain buffers. {them_first} wins this one.

setups.title: On the number line
text: {period}, {class_name}. {teacher} sticks cards on the board: fractions, decimals, a square root. "Number line. Smallest first."
{period}. "Quick one," {teacher} says. "Put these in order. Negatives count."
great: Every one in place. {teacher}: "That's the lesson. We can go home."
Clean. Even the square root.
miss: Two-thirds and three-quarters swap places in your head every time.
The negative number gets you. It always gets someone.

setups.title: Stop the pendulum
text: {period}, {class_name}. {teacher} sets a pendulum swinging. "Stop it at the bottom of the swing. Dead center."
{period}. {teacher} hands you the stopwatch trigger. "Catch it at the lowest point. That's the whole experiment."
setups.how: Tap to stop it in the zone.
great: Right at the bottom, three times. {teacher} writes your data on the board as the example.
Perfect timing. Your lab data is the cleanest in the room.
good: A little early, a little late. Averages out.
miss: Your data looks like a seismograph.
{them_first} takes the trigger back. "Let me."

setups.title: Catch the ruler
text: {period}, {class_name}. Rulers, partners. "Your partner drops it, you catch it, we figure out your reaction time." {them_first} is holding yours.
{period}. {teacher} demonstrates with a meter stick. "Thumb and finger ready. When it drops, you grab."
great: You catch it almost before it moves. {them_first}: "Okay, cheater."
Fastest hands in the room. It goes on the board.
good: Middle of the pack. Human, basically.
miss: It hits the floor. Twice. {them_first} is crying laughing.
You grab air. The ruler grabs nothing.

setups.title: Planets in order
text: {period}, {class_name}. {teacher} hands out planet cards. "From the Sun, out. Go."
{period}. "Solar system speed round," {teacher} says. "Closest to the Sun first."
setups.how: Tap them closest to the Sun first.
great: Clean. {teacher} gives your table first pick of seats for the video.
All of them. You didn't even hesitate.
miss: You put Saturn next to the Sun. You'll hear about it.
{them_first} fixes it for you, very slowly, while making eye contact.

setups.title: Slowest to fastest
text: {period}, {class_name}. "Speed round," {teacher} says, dealing cards. "Slowest to fastest."
{period}. {teacher}: "Snail to light. Order them by speed. You versus {them_first}."
great: Every one in place. Sound before light, obviously.
Clean. {teacher}: "Somebody was listening."
good: One swap. The jetliner and sound are close.
miss: You make the cheetah faster than sound. It is not.
{them_first}: "Light is the fast one. Always light."

setups.title: Find the typo
text: {period}, {class_name}. {teacher} puts a slide up. "There's a typo in here. First to find it picks the reading order."
{period}. "Proofreading drill," {teacher} says. "One's wrong. Find it."
setups.how: Tap the one that's spelled wrong.
great: Got it before anyone else. You pick the reading order, and you pick yourself last.
Three for three. {teacher}: "Editor."
good: Two out of three. The double letters got you.
miss: All of them look wrong now. That's what happens when you stare at a word.
You tap the right spelling. Confidently.

setups.title: ABC order
text: {period}, {class_name}. {teacher} hands out vocab cards. "Alphabetical. Fast. Winner picks Friday's book."
{period}. "Warm-up," {teacher} says. "Put these in ABC order. They all start the same, so read carefully."
great: Flawless. You pick Friday's book.
{teacher} checks it twice. "Perfect."
miss: You forget how the alphabet goes, briefly, at sixteen.
{them_first}: "You good?"

setups.title: Timeline
text: {period}, {class_name}. {teacher} deals event cards facedown. "Oldest to newest. You've got seconds."
{period}. "Timeline race," {teacher} says. "You versus {them_first}. Flip and go."
great: Every date in place. {teacher}: "You've been reading."
You beat {them_first} by a mile.
good: One swap. The middle ones are always close.
miss: You put the Moon landing before the Civil War. Bold.
Centuries are just numbers. Big ones.

setups.title: Hand up first
text: {period}, {class_name}. {teacher}: "First hand up after I finish the question gets to answer."
{period}. Review game. Fastest hand gets the point. {them_first} is already leaning forward.
setups.how: Wait for it. Tap the instant it goes.
great: Your hand's up before the question ends. Fastest in the room, three times.
You beat {them_first} every time. They're furious. It's great.
good: You get one in. Good enough.
miss: You jump the gun. {teacher}: "I hadn't asked anything yet."
{them_first} is faster. Every time.

setups.title: ¿Dónde está el acento?
text: {period}, {class_name}. {teacher} flashes the same word over and over. "¿Cuál no tiene acento?"
{period}. "Uno está mal," says {teacher}. "Find the one missing its accent."
setups.how: Tap the one missing its accent.
great: ¡Perfecto! {teacher} gives you a sticker. You're keeping the sticker.
Three for three. "Muy bien," says {teacher}.
miss: The accents all blur together.
{teacher}: "Casi." You'll take casi.

setups.title: Números
text: {period}, {class_name}. "Del más pequeño al más grande," says {teacher}, tossing number cards on your desk.
{period}. {teacher} holds up number words. "In order. Rápido."
great: ¡Perfecto! Even quince.
{teacher}: "Excelente."
good: One swap. Doce and dos are a trap.
miss: Cincuenta and cinco look like the same number when you panic.
{them_first} whispers "veinte es twenty" one second too late.

setups.title: Quick hands
text: {period}, {class_name}. Reaction drills. {teacher} holds a tennis ball at shoulder height. "When I drop it, you grab it."
{period}. Gym. {teacher} lines everyone up. "Grab it before it bounces twice. Ready."
great: You snatch it every time. {teacher}: "Somebody's been training."
Fastest hands in the gym.
miss: The ball bounces off your wrist and rolls under the bleachers.
{them_first} catches yours too. Rude.

setups.title: Power throw
text: {period}, {class_name}. {teacher} rolls out the medicine balls. "Wind up, let it go at the right moment. Distance counts."
{period}. Throw test. Hold the wind-up, let it go in the sweet spot. {them_first} went first and set the mark.
setups.how: Hold to wind up. Let go in the green.
great: It sails past the cone. {teacher} has to go get it.
You beat {them_first}'s mark. They want a rematch.
miss: It goes about four feet. Straight down.
You let go way too early. Everyone ducks.

setups.title: Jump in
text: {period}, {class_name}. Double-dutch day. {them_first} is turning. You have to jump in at the right moment.
{period}. Jump rope relay. Time it right or eat the rope.
setups.how: Tap when it's in the zone.
great: You jump in like you've done this your whole life.
Perfect rhythm. {them_first} speeds it up just to mess with you, and you still make it.
miss: The rope wins.
You stop it with your face. Gently. Mostly.

setups.title: Off by a shade
text: {period}, {class_name}. {teacher} holds up a swatch card. "One of these is mixed wrong. Find it."
{period}. Color theory. "Train your eye," says {teacher}. "One's off."
great: You see it instantly. {teacher}: "Good eye."
Three for three. Even the subtle one.
good: Two of three. The last one was mean.
miss: Every square is the same square. You'd swear to it.
You pick the right color. The one that was right, that is.

setups.title: One steady stroke
text: {period}, {class_name}. {teacher}: "One brushstroke. Start to finish. Stop right on the line."
{period}. Ink warm-up. One pull of the brush, and you have to stop on the mark.
setups.how: Hold to draw. Let go on the line.
great: Clean line, clean stop. {teacher} pins it up.
Perfect. You'd frame it.
good: A little long, but it's got character.
miss: Your line goes off the page and onto the table.
{them_first}: "It's abstract."

setups.title: Color order
text: {period}, {class_name}. Paint cups everywhere. "Rainbow order," says {teacher}. "Go."
{period}. {teacher} scatters swatches. "In order, like the rainbow."
great: Clean. Even indigo.
Perfect.
good: Indigo and violet swapped. Everyone does that.
miss: You put green first. Bold choice.
{them_first}: "Roy G. Biv, man."

setups.title: On the beat
text: {period}, {class_name}. {teacher} starts the metronome. "Hit the downbeat. Not before, not after."
{period}. Rhythm check. One at a time, you hit the beat while everyone listens.
setups.how: Tap when it's in the zone.
great: Right in the pocket. {teacher} points at you with the baton.
Perfect time. Even {them_first} nods.
miss: You rush it. Then you drag it. Then you rush it.
{teacher}: "Feel it, don't think it."

setups.title: Play it back
text: {period}, {class_name}. {teacher} plays a short pattern on the keys. "Play it back."
{period}. Ear training. {teacher} plays it once. Only once.
setups.how: Watch the pattern, then tap it back.
great: Every note. {teacher}: "You've got an ear."
Perfect playback. The room goes quiet for a second.
good: Most of it. Lost the last note.
miss: You play something. It is not what {teacher} played.
Your hands forget halfway through.

setups.title: Slow to fast
text: {period}, {class_name}. {teacher} holds up tempo cards. "Slowest to fastest. Go."
{period}. Music theory sprint. "Largo to presto," {teacher} says. "In order."
great: Perfect. {teacher}: "Allegro."
Every one.
good: One swap. Andante and adagio look alike.
miss: Presto first. Sure.
{them_first}: "Largo means slow, dude."

setups.title: Longest to shortest
text: {period}, {class_name}. Note values. "Longest first," says {teacher}.
{period}. Theory sprint: whole notes down to sixteenths. Longest first.
great: Perfect. {teacher} taps the music stand twice. Approval.
Every one.
good: One swap. Eighths and sixteenths blur.
miss: You make the sixteenth note the long one.
{them_first}: "Whole note. Four beats. Come on."

setups.title: Binary
text: {period}, {class_name}. {teacher} puts binary numbers on the board. "Smallest to largest. No converting out loud."
{period}. "Warm-up," {teacher} says. "These are in binary. Order them."
setups.how: Tap them smallest first. They're binary.
great: Clean. {teacher}: "Zero bugs."
Every one, first try.
good: One off by a bit. Literally.
miss: Ones and zeros. So many ones and zeros.
{them_first}: "It's base two, bro."

setups.title: Repeat the pattern
text: {period}, {class_name}. {teacher} lights up a pattern on the board. "Repeat it. Exactly."
{period}. Memory test. "The average person holds about seven things at once," says {teacher}. "Let's see."
setups.how: Watch the pattern, then tap it back.
great: Every square. {teacher} raises an eyebrow.
Perfect recall. Above average, officially.
miss: It's gone the second it stops.
You remember the first two. Great first two.

setups.title: Time the signal
text: {period}, {class_name}. {teacher}'s demo: "Tap when the signal's in the window. Too early or late and the packet drops."
{period}. Timing lab. Hit the window, three times.
setups.how: Tap to stop it in the zone.
great: Zero packets dropped.
Perfect timing, three for three.
miss: Connection lost.
{them_first}: "Have you tried turning it off and on?"

setups.title: Reaction test
text: {period}, {class_name}. Today's experiment: reaction time. "Tap the instant it turns green," says {teacher}.
{period}. Lab day. You're the subject. {them_first} is recording.
great: Your times are the fastest in the class. You're an outlier, scientifically.
Lightning. {them_first} checks the timer twice.
miss: You jump early. That's a data point too.
Slow. You blame the coffee you didn't have.

setups.title: Make change
text: {period}, {class_name}. {teacher} runs a register drill. "Customer pays, you make change. Fast."
{period}. Price check. "Tips, change, discounts. Go," says {teacher}.
great: Every one to the cent. {teacher}: "Hired."
Perfect. You'd make a great cashier and a better accountant.
good: Pretty good. One customer got shorted a quarter.
miss: You give someone eleven dollars in change for a ten.
The math is easy. The pressure isn't.

setups.title: Lightning round
text: {period}, {class_name}. Ten minutes left. {teacher} pulls out a stack of questions. "Lightning round. Three questions."
{period}. "Pop review," {teacher} says. "Three quick ones. You versus {them_first}."
great: Three for three. {teacher} gives you the nod.
You beat {them_first} clean.
miss: Your mind goes completely blank. Like, white noise.
{them_first} gets every one you miss.
